chapter: Joe Liggins and back to Kid Ory
title: Ory's band: professional, no jam sessions
summary: The Ory band did no day jobs after becoming successful and rarely jammed, except at Buster's house.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Was the Ory band totally what you might call a professional band, I mean, in the respect that none of them did day jobs when they got more famous...
None of them did any day jobs after we got going.
They didn't need to. Because we made fairly good money -- for a long time.
How did they feel about playing for free, like jam sessions? Would they do anything like that, or would they just work when the pay was there? Ory's band.
Come to think about it, I guess we played a few benefits. But it wasn't any...
I didn't mean sort of organized that there was no charge and the band donated time. I mean jam sessions. Did you have many of those kinds of things with Ory's band?
No, not really. Ory never was a guy for anything like that. At one time we had some jam sessions at the Beverly Cavern.
But I mean, it wasn't the kind of band where some of you might go to a party at someone's house and play, and this kind of stuff -- there was very little of that going on?

I used to do a lot of it. And I can't remember Ram doing...and Frank... Well, Frank Passley wasn't in the band anyway. But I'm trying to think... Well, at Buster's house... That's where we all gathered. Buster used to live at 53rd and Central, and that's where... A lot of musicians when they'd would get off from work would go over
to Buster's house, and even in the daytime, when we were in the Kid Ory band, until Buster died. And after that, I can't remember guys just having sessions. Everybody went their own way, you know.

No one has ever sort of brought that out about Ory's band. The George Lewis band, which was going around the same time, you often see tapes of them at parties with different musicians, and playing with young guys, different players -- Johnny Williams sometimes would come play trumpet at a jam session. But Ory... I've very seldom heard any tapes or recordings of anything. So you were corroborating that it was a band mostly, then, that sort of stayed to itself, and played professionally when it was working, and then didn't socialize a whole lot.
